title: Correctness: ioctl_key_generate leaves inbuf uncleared on pre-lock errors
description: Trigger: user calls write(fd, sensitive_bytes, n) on an UNSET fd, then calls KEY_GENERATE with a bad arg pointer (copy_from_user fails), or with an empty algo string (line 2128), or with nonzero _pad (line 2131). All three exit paths return before acquiring state->lock and without calling inbuf_clear. The sensitive write() data remains in state->inbuf until fd close(). Contrast with ioctl_key_import which explicitly acquires the lock and calls inbuf_clear() on copy_from_user failure (lines 1712-1714). FIPS 140-3 requires CSPs to be zeroized when no longer operationally needed. A KEY_GENERATE failure leaves key material from a prior write() in inbuf for the lifetime of the fd. The EBUSY path (line 2139) correctly calls inbuf_clear; the pre-lock paths do not.
